clue.text: Might he ply his craft between Flint and Wick?

definitions.text: Might he ply his craft between Flint and Wick?

parts.words: Might he ply his craft between Flint and Wick?
parts.note: Flint and Wick read as places suggest a boatman working a coastal route, but flint and wick are the parts of a cigarette lighter, so the craft is a lighter barge

explanation.surface: A boatman working the coast between the Welsh town of Flint and the Scottish port of Wick.
explanation.walkthrough: Flint (north Wales) and Wick (Caithness) are real towns; a lighter is also a flat-bottomed barge, and its operator works one for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighterman operates a lighter, a barge used to ferry cargo between ships and the quay.

clue.text: Instrument which does not sound true

definitions.meaning: a small harp of ancient Greece
said aloud it sounds like a liar, someone whose words are untrue

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that plays out of tune.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient harp is a stringed instrument, and its name is said like someone who tells falsehoods.

clue.text: Open wide breach to the east

parts.note: a breach is a gap in a wall or defence
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A wide breach opening up on the eastern side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' simply links: GAP has E added after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to open the mouth wide, as in a yawn.

clue.text: Their get-together is an annual affair

definitions.text: Their get-together is an annual affair

parts.words: Their get-together is an annual affair
parts.note: suggests a yearly reunion of a club, but means the parts of the calendar which together make up a year

explanation.surface: A society whose reunion is held once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelvemonth is an old word for a year, made up of its twelve months.

clue.text: 21 from trees seeming to go wrong again

parts.note: RE is a prefix meaning again
to sin is to go wrong morally

explanation.surface: Something emerging from trees that seems to go astray once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is ISSUE: resin issues, or oozes, from trees. 'seeming to' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the sticky sap that exudes from pine and other trees.

clue.text: Modern tan a form of this

definitions.text: Modern tan a form of this

indicators.note: a form of means the preceding words are reshaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A modern suntan is a type of decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges MODERN TAN; read as a whole, a fashionable tan is a way of beautifying oneself. The OCR read 'tan' as 'can'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adornment is decoration of the body, and a suntan is one cosmetic kind.

clue.text: Complaint of weird sister going topless

indicators.note: losing the top means the first letter of the word for the weird sister is dropped

parts.note: the Weird Sisters are the three witches in Shakespeare's Macbeth, so one of them is a witch

explanation.surface: One of Macbeth's witches grumbles about going without a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' removes the first letter W from WITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a minor ailment or skin irritation, a complaint in the medical sense.

clue.text: The newcomer is sensitive in the extreme

parts.note: tender means sore and sensitive to touch
the foot is the extremity of the body or the bottom end of anything

explanation.surface: A new arrival who is extremely touchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderfoot is a novice or inexperienced new arrival, originally on the American frontier.

clue.text: Requirement for dealing with pupils so strong-willed

definitions.meaning: a school's head teacher needs to be robust, so the phrase is the head plus strong
obstinate and determined to get one's way

explanation.surface: A teacher needs a forceful personality to manage a class.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilful obstinate person insists on their own way, and a head teacher must be firm.

clue.text: Strangely, it may make a person rise

definitions.text: Strangely, it may make a person rise

indicators.note: strangely means the following letters are put into a strange, new order

explanation.surface: An odd observation that something can make a person get up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges PERSON RISE; read as a whole, harsh suppression may well provoke a person to rise in revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Repression is forcible suppression of people, which can provoke them to rebel or rise up.

clue.text: " Great! whom three realms obey" (Pope)

parts.note: a line from Pope's The Rape of the Lock with the queen's name left out, addressed to the monarch who ruled England, Scotland and Ireland

explanation.surface: A quotation from Alexander Pope praising a monarch obeyed by three kingdoms.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue had a dash after 'Great' marking the gap; the line is 'Here thou, great Anna! whom three realms obey', addressed to Queen Anne.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope used the Latinate form of Queen Anne's name for the sovereign of England, Scotland and Ireland.

clue.text: They keep meetings in suspense, as it were

definitions.text: They keep meetings in suspense, as it were

parts.words: They keep meetings in suspense, as it were
parts.note: suggests dramatic tension at a gathering, but means suspending sessions until a later date

explanation.surface: Things that keep a meeting on tenterhooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjourning a meeting suspends it so that it resumes later.

clue.text: Tailors have no alternative, they're essential to it

definitions.text: Tailors have no alternative, they're essential to it

parts.words: Tailors have no alternative, they're essential to it
parts.note: take the word for alternative, or, out of tailors to leave tails, and tails are an essential part of formal evening wear

explanation.surface: Clothiers insist there is no other option for a formal outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailors' without OR (alternative) leaves TAILS, the tailcoat worn with white tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal evening dress for men is white tie, which means a tailcoat.

clue.text: Objects are to be found in this case

definitions.text: Objects are to be found in this case

parts.words: Objects are to be found in this case
parts.note: suggests things in a display cabinet, but means the grammatical case for the object of a verb

explanation.surface: A display case where objects are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the accusative is the case marking the direct object of a verb.

clue.text: Malapropian allegories

parts.note: Mrs Malaprop in Sheridan's The Rivals speaks of an allegory on the banks of the Nile, confusing two similar words

explanation.surface: Symbolic tales told in muddled language.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Malaprop's line is 'as headstrong as an allegory on the banks of the Nile', meaning the reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: The reptile word is what Mrs Malaprop mangled into allegory, a classic malapropism.

clue.text: Pantomime character in the garden

definitions.meaning: Harlequin's sweetheart in the traditional harlequinade of pantomime
a garden flower, the aquilegia, also called granny's bonnet

explanation.surface: A pantomime performer appearing in a garden scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the harlequinade heroine and the aquilegia flower share this name.

clue.text: She loves an aroma with it cooking '

indicators.note: cooking means the preceding letters are being stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman who loves the smell of food being prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges AN AROMA IT; 'loves' and 'with' are link words, though the beloved woman hints at love too.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female lover or sweetheart, a woman.

clue.text: Present of 24 in France

parts.note: the answer to 24 across is the metal, and fer is French for that metal

explanation.surface: A gift of a golf club received in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to proffer it, a verb sense shared with hold out.

clue.text: Often hoisted with a jack

parts.note: a jack suggests lifting a car, but the flag of the United Kingdom is called a jack and often flown

explanation.surface: Something regularly lifted using a car jack.
explanation.definitionFit: The Union Jack is the national flag of the UK, hoisted on flagpoles.

clue.text: When the Prime Minister is shortly to appear?

definitions.text: When the Prime Minister is shortly to appear?

parts.words: When the Prime Minister is shortly to appear?
parts.note: Prime Minister is shortened to PM, and PM also means the time after midday

explanation.surface: Asking at what time the head of government is due to turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: PM stands for post meridiem, the part of the day after noon.

clue.text: Cases of mixed dates

parts.note: suggests boxes of assorted fruit, but means instances where things from different periods are put together

explanation.surface: Boxes of assorted dates from a grocer.
explanation.definitionFit: An anachronism places something in the wrong period, confusing times.

clue.text: Publisher's children ?

definitions.meaning: what a publisher produces, an edition or number of a magazine
offspring, as in died without children

explanation.surface: A publisher's children.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition put out by a publisher, and offspring in law, share this word.

clue.text: The one to consult as a matter of course

definitions.text: The one to consult as a matter of course

parts.words: The one to consult as a matter of course
parts.note: suggests an adviser one routinely checks with, but means the card listing the courses of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone you always check with by habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu lists the dishes, course by course, available at a meal.

clue.text: It's always fair in weather reports for shipping

definitions.text: It's always fair in weather reports for shipping

parts.words: It's always fair in weather reports for shipping
parts.note: the BBC shipping forecast names a sea area Fair ..., so that place is always fair whatever the weather

explanation.surface: The shipping forecast always predicting fine weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shipping Forecast is a BBC radio weather bulletin for sea areas around Britain; Fair Isle, between Orkney and Shetland, is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair Isle is a small island, and gives its name to a shipping forecast area.

clue.text: Old soldier without side in the club

indicators.note: without tells us the next word is taken away from the soldier's name

parts.note: Ironsides were Cromwell's cavalry troopers in the English Civil War
taken as written

explanation.surface: A veteran soldier sitting in his club with no one on his side.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromwell's cavalry were called Ironsides; 'without' strips SIDE from IRONSIDE. 'in the' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, an iron is a type of club with a metal head.

clue.text: They get carried away

parts.note: suggests people overcome by emotion, but means people transported by a vehicle

explanation.surface: People who let their enthusiasm run away with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers are travellers conveyed by bus, train or ship to somewhere else.

clue.text: Soldiers stand it, so it can't be hard

definitions.meaning: the drill command 'stand at ease', relaxing on parade

explanation.surface: Troops on parade put up with something, so it must be simple.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Stand easy' is a parade command, and something not difficult is simple.

clue.text: Relish for mutton, or for the dance?

definitions.text: Relish for mutton, or for the dance?

parts.words: Relish for mutton, or for the dance?
parts.note: a condiment made from pickled flower buds traditionally served with lamb, also read as cheek or enthusiasm for a lively frisky leap

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sauce goes with mutton or whether someone has a taste for dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: A caper is both a pickled bud and a playful leap; sauce is also cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: This condiment of pickled caper buds is the classic accompaniment to boiled mutton.
